# Schema.org

*Standard*

The shared vocabulary of types and properties that structured data uses, launched by the major search engines in 2011.

**Glossary** (*Schema.org*): The shared markup vocabulary that major search engines announced together in June 2011; Google uses only the subsets its documentation declares.

Narrative: the topic [Schema.org vocabulary](../topics/schema-org.md) tells the story; this card lists what links to it.

30 claims mention it: 4 from Google's documentation, 19 shown or said at the event (11 not in Google docs, 3 confirmed by Google docs, 4 consistent with Google docs, 1 nothing to verify), 7 the author's analysis. A card is a map: cite the claim ids, with the citation given after each claim.

## Google's documentation

Documented in: [Introducing schema.org: Search engines come together for a richer web](https://developers.google.com/search/blog/2011/06/introducing-schemaorg-search-engines).

- [`D2-C480`](../sessions/D2-S12-what-is-structured-data-and-why-we-need-it-on-the-internet.md) Docs: Google's guide to optimizing for generative AI features lists 'overfocusing on structured data' among the things site owners don't need to do: structured data is not required for generative AI search and no special schema.org markup is needed, though it remains worth using because it helps pages become eligible for rich results. `[D2-C480, docs, Google Search Central, https://developers.google.com/search/docs/fundamentals/ai-optimization-guide]`
- [`D3-C227`](../sessions/D3-S06-uncovering-trustworthy-experiences-on-discover.md) Docs: Google's Discover documentation says to specify the large image with schema.org markup or the og:image meta tag, which can influence the thumbnail Discover chooses, and that a vertical image cropped to 16x9 must keep its important details. `[D3-C227, docs, Google Search Central, https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/google-discover]`
- [`D3-C326`](../sessions/D3-S10-how-search-results-are-born.md) Docs: Google's AI features guide says there are no additional requirements, and no special schema.org structured data, needed to appear in AI Overviews or AI Mode; a page must be indexed and eligible to be shown with a snippet. `[D3-C326, docs, Google Search Central, https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/ai-features]`
- [`D3-C347`](../sessions/D3-S10-how-search-results-are-born.md) Docs: Google's Merchant Center help says products and details crawled from an online store can show up on Google even when they are not marked up with schema.org or added in Merchant Center, and lists the Shopping tab among the places Merchant Center free listings appear. `[D3-C347, docs, Google Merchant Center Help, https://support.google.com/merchants/answer/9199328?hl=en]`

## Shown or said at the event

Not in Google's documentation first: present those as said at Search Central Live, never as documented policy.

- [`D2-C460`](../sessions/D2-S12-what-is-structured-data-and-why-we-need-it-on-the-internet.md) Stage, Day 2, not in Google docs: In the speaker's own tests, even the latest LLMs asked to generate schema.org markup for a page often invent properties that do not exist, get deeply nested schemas such as complex pricing models wrong, and duplicate content across several fields. `[D2-C460, stage, Google, Day 2]`
- [`D2-C477`](../sessions/D2-S12-what-is-structured-data-and-why-we-need-it-on-the-internet.md) Stage, Day 2, not in Google docs: As far as the speaker knows, in most of Google's main AI uses a page's schema.org markup is not turned into text and put directly into the model's context; the data is first sorted out, checked for quality and indexed before it is passed on as grounding context. `[D2-C477, stage, Google, Day 2]`
- [`D2-C478`](../sessions/D2-S12-what-is-structured-data-and-why-we-need-it-on-the-internet.md) Stage, Day 2, not in Google docs: The speaker said there are concerns that feeding raw schema.org markup straight into an AI model's context would be a big abuse vector, one reason Google does not do so. `[D2-C478, stage, Google, Day 2]`
- [`D2-C510`](../sessions/D2-S12-what-is-structured-data-and-why-we-need-it-on-the-internet.md) Stage, Day 2, not in Google docs: Schema.org, in which Google is a major participant, began publishing usage statistics for all its types and properties in 2026, showing in buckets how many domains use each one; the data is also in schema.org's GitHub repository. `[D2-C510, stage, Google, Day 2]`
- [`D2-C511`](../sessions/D2-S12-what-is-structured-data-and-why-we-need-it-on-the-internet.md) Stage, Day 2, not in Google docs: Google often needs to see a markup type adopted on websites before it invests in a feature that uses it, a chicken-and-egg problem that the schema.org usage statistics are meant to help break. `[D2-C511, stage, Google, Day 2]`
- [`D2-C512`](../sessions/D2-S12-what-is-structured-data-and-why-we-need-it-on-the-internet.md) Stage, Day 2, not in Google docs: Schema.org added support for RDF lists and sets, which give a way to express ordered values, because RDF triples are not ordered by nature. `[D2-C512, stage, Google, Day 2]`
- [`D3-C353`](../sessions/D3-S11-shopping-on-search-beyond-the-blue-links.md) Stage, Day 3, not in Google docs: Schema.org product markup on websites is another source of billions of product offers for Google Shopping, next to merchant feeds. `[D3-C353, stage, Alex Jansen, Day 3]`
- [`D3-C380`](../sessions/D3-S11-shopping-on-search-beyond-the-blue-links.md) Stage, Day 3, not in Google docs: Most of the new conversational feed attributes were already available in schema.org, so Google ties them back to structured data and can use them from product markup as well as from feeds. `[D3-C380, stage, Alex Jansen, Day 3]`
- [`D3-C391`](../sessions/D3-S11-shopping-on-search-beyond-the-blue-links.md) Stage, Day 3, not in Google docs: Product Q&A can be marked up in schema.org by linking Question items, each with an acceptedAnswer of type Answer, to the product through the subjectOf property, because the product is the subject of the Q&A. `[D3-C391, stage, Alex Jansen, Day 3]`
- [`D3-C399`](../sessions/D3-S11-shopping-on-search-beyond-the-blue-links.md) Stage, Day 3, not in Google docs: A recent schema.org release added two properties, specification and valueGroup, so that the Merchant Center product detail attribute can be expressed in schema.org, with product specs nested under specification. `[D3-C399, stage, Alex Jansen, Day 3]`
- [`D3-C403`](../sessions/D3-S11-shopping-on-search-beyond-the-blue-links.md) Stage, Day 3, not in Google docs: Rich, less structured product data that is not prescribed by Google, schema.org or any feed or data model is increasingly important, because the merchant or brand knows best what to provide. `[D3-C403, stage, Alex Jansen, Day 3]`
- [`D2-C484`](../sessions/D2-S12-what-is-structured-data-and-why-we-need-it-on-the-internet.md) Stage, Day 2, confirmed by Google docs: Schema.org is a common vocabulary that several major search engines started together so that site owners can mark up pages and every consumer interprets the markup the same way; the speaker put its start 15 to 20 years ago (Google, Bing and Yahoo! announced it in June 2011). `[D2-C484, stage, Google, Day 2]`
- [`D3-C354`](../sessions/D3-S11-shopping-on-search-beyond-the-blue-links.md) Stage, Day 3, confirmed by Google docs: Product snippets in Google Search are powered by both shopping feeds and schema.org structured data. `[D3-C354, stage, Alex Jansen, Day 3]`
- [`D3-C407`](../sessions/D3-S11-shopping-on-search-beyond-the-blue-links.md) Stage, Day 3, confirmed by Google docs: Google Shopping pointed to a Google holiday shopping blog post with early results from real merchants using the conversational attributes, and to the Merchant Center Help Center and schema.org for the attributes and properties. `[D3-C407, stage, Alex Jansen, Day 3]`
- [`D2-C486`](../sessions/D2-S12-what-is-structured-data-and-why-we-need-it-on-the-internet.md) Stage, Day 2, consistent with Google docs: Marking something up with only a very generic schema.org type says little about it and is very hard for Google to use. `[D2-C486, stage, Google, Day 2]`
- [`D2-C487`](../sessions/D2-S12-what-is-structured-data-and-why-we-need-it-on-the-internet.md) Stage, Day 2, consistent with Google docs: Google uses schema.org as its markup vocabulary but mostly consumes only the subsets that its developer documentation declares, for the features it builds. `[D2-C487, stage, Google, Day 2]`
- [`D3-C396`](../sessions/D3-S11-shopping-on-search-beyond-the-blue-links.md) Stage, Day 3, consistent with Google docs: Google works to make sure that what merchants can express in its shopping feeds can also be expressed in schema.org, adding vocabulary where schema.org lacks it, for example for product details. `[D3-C396, stage, Alex Jansen, Day 3]`
- [`D3-C397`](../sessions/D3-S11-shopping-on-search-beyond-the-blue-links.md) Stage, Day 3, consistent with Google docs: Google named the Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP), next to the Merchant Center feed, as an industry standard whose capabilities it also wants schema.org to cover. `[D3-C397, stage, Alex Jansen, Day 3]`
- [`D2-C485`](../sessions/D2-S12-what-is-structured-data-and-why-we-need-it-on-the-internet.md) Stage, Day 2, nothing to verify: Schema.org is an open public collaboration, and the speaker invited people who enjoy ontologies and data to join it. `[D2-C485, stage, Google, Day 2]`

## The author's analysis

- [`D1-C315`](../sessions/D1-S04-lightning-session-a-automation-and-ai.md) Analysis: Google's AI optimisation guide says structured data is not required for generative AI search and needs no special schema.org markup, and on Day 2 Google said raw schema.org is generally not put into model context (D2-C477); use markup for rich-result eligibility and clear data, not as an AI-visibility lever. `[D1-C315, analysis, Ibrahim Anjro]`
- [`D2-C479`](../sessions/D2-S12-what-is-structured-data-and-why-we-need-it-on-the-internet.md) Analysis: There is no separate markup for AI features: by Google's account the same processed markup feeds classic results and AI answers, and raw schema.org is generally not passed into model context, so invest in the types Google documents for its features rather than in extra markup written for AI. `[D2-C479, analysis, Ibrahim Anjro]`
- [`D2-C513`](../sessions/D2-S12-what-is-structured-data-and-why-we-need-it-on-the-internet.md) Analysis: Markup for schema.org types that Google does not use yet is a bet on future features; check a type's usage bucket on schema.org before investing, since adoption is what Google says it watches before building a feature. `[D2-C513, analysis, Ibrahim Anjro]`
- [`D3-C230`](../sessions/D3-S06-uncovering-trustworthy-experiences-on-discover.md) Analysis: For Discover, set max-image-preview:large on article templates, give every article a relevant image at least 1,200 px wide in og:image or schema.org markup that is neither the site logo nor text-heavy, and show clear bylines and dates. `[D3-C230, analysis, Ibrahim Anjro]`
- [`D3-C381`](../sessions/D3-S11-shopping-on-search-beyond-the-blue-links.md) Analysis: As of 3 October 2026 Google's Merchant Center help lists no schema.org property for question_and_answer, document_link, related_product, popularity_rank, variant_option or product_detail (only item_group_title maps, to ProductGroup.name), and Search Central does not document such markup: reading these attributes from schema.org is a stage statement, the feed is the documented route. `[D3-C381, analysis, Ibrahim Anjro]`
- [`D3-C400`](../sessions/D3-S11-shopping-on-search-beyond-the-blue-links.md) Analysis: Schema.org's release notes show version 30.1 (16 September 2026) added specification, isOftenBoughtWith and consumerNotice for Product, valueGroup for PropertyValue and itemPopularity for Offer as vocabulary for retail feed data; Google's Search Central docs did not yet document these properties on 3 October 2026. `[D3-C400, analysis, Ibrahim Anjro]`
- [`D3-C410`](../sessions/D3-S11-shopping-on-search-beyond-the-blue-links.md) Analysis: Shop developers should first keep core feed and markup values (price, availability, brand, GTIN) accurate, then add Q&As, product highlights, specs as key-value product details and related products in the Merchant Center feed, and mirror them in schema.org Product markup only as Google documents support for it. `[D3-C410, analysis, Ibrahim Anjro]`

## For developers

- `DEV-AIF-02` **SHOULD** · Documented: Spend no effort on llms.txt, AI text files or AI-specific markup for Google (3 of its claims mention it)
- `DEV-IMG-07` **SHOULD** · Documented: Give every article a large, relevant lead image and declare it in og:image or markup (2 of its claims mention it; its own text names it)
- `DEV-SDA-03` **SHOULD** · Documented: Choose the specific types Google documents for its features, and skip generic or irrelevant ones (2 of its claims mention it; its own text names it)
- `DEV-SHP-04` **MAY** · Said at Search Central Live: Treat product Q&A and specification markup in schema.org as an extra on top of the feed (5 of its claims mention it; its own text names it)
